name: Godspeed You! Black Emperor
label: Constellation
lede: A Montreal collective with no singer and no use for your approval makes hour-long records about the end of the world, gets held by the FBI at an Oklahoma gas station, and calls the gala that just handed it a prize insane.

eras.title: Five hundred copies and a loft
eras.text: Godspeed starts as three people in Montreal and grows into a shifting crowd of guitars, strings and tape. The first real record is pressed in a run of 500 and assembled by the band by hand.

years.h: A support slot for Steak 72 turns into Godspeed
years.p: Efrim Menuck, Mike Moya and Mauro Pezzente form the band in Montreal. The name comes from Mitsuo Yanagimachi's 1976 Japanese documentary about the Black Emperors biker gang.

years.h: The first cassette becomes the thing fans hunt for
years.p: Efrim Menuck makes a tiny-run tape, All Lights Fucked on the Hairy Amp Drooling, with help from Mauro Pezzente. For almost three decades it is the most hunted-after object in the band's world.
years.xp: The tape stayed mostly theoretical for fans until February 2022, when a copy surfaced on 4chan's /mu/ board. On February 14, 2022 the band put the full audio up on its own Bandcamp.

years.src: Wikipedia: F♯ A♯ ∞ · Wikipedia: Efrim Menuck
years.h: A Mile End loft that used to be a gallery becomes the studio
years.p: Godspeed records its debut, F♯ A♯ ∞, in May 1997 at Hotel2Tango, formerly Gallery Quiva. Efrim Menuck had set the room up as a studio around 1996.

years.h: Five hundred LPs, each with a penny a train flattened
years.p: Constellation releases F♯ A♯ ∞ as CST003, hand-packaged and numbered. Each jacket has one of three photos glued on by hand, and the envelope inside holds a handbill, a Menuck drawing and a Canadian penny flattened by a train.
years.xp:
The jackets were made by the band, the label and Montreal artists, with a watertower, a train or a road sign photo stuck on each. A silk-screened image honors blues musician Reverend Gary Davis. The vinyl ends in a locked groove, which is why the running time is written as infinity.

The spoken opening of "The Dead Flag Blues" came from an unfinished screenplay by Menuck. Later pressings swap in a US penny, since Canada stopped minting them.

eras.title: Kranky takes the tapes south
eras.text: The band mailed the LP to Chicago's Kranky hoping for help touring the States, and Kranky put it out on CD. Over the next four years a nine-piece Godspeed became the reference point for orchestral post-rock, and the politics got louder with every sleeve.

years.h: Kranky answers the mailed LP with a US CD
years.p: Chicago's Kranky issues it as krank 027: 63 minutes against the LP's 38, with reworked sections and new material. The CD lands fourth in The Wire's 1998 critics' poll.
years.xp: The band had sent the LP to Kranky hoping for help touring the US. The label's answer was a CD of its own, so the American version of the record is a different, longer one than the 500 hand-packaged Montreal copies.

years.h: Mike Moya leaves for HṚṢṬA; Fly Pan Am's guitarist steps in
years.p: Roger Tellier-Craig of [[Fly Pan Am|c191214c-31e6-4d26-bfa7-35be4d90d178]] takes the guitar, and Godspeed settles into a nine-piece that starts touring.

years.cap: Hebrew on the front, Italian on the back
years.src: Wikipedia: Slow Riot for New Zerø Kanada
years.h: The Slow Riot EP names the band nowhere on its packaging
years.p: The front reads Tohu VaVohu in Hebrew, the case opens backwards, and the back carries Italian instructions for making a Molotov cocktail.
years.xp: "Moya" is named for Mike Moya and reworks a Górecki symphony. "BBF3" is built around a street interview with a man calling himself Blaise Bailey Finnegan III, whose poem borrows from Iron Maiden. Dale Morningstar recorded it at The Gas Station in Toronto.

years.cap: The band live in London, November 2000
years.h: Godspeed cuts Lift Your Skinny Fists in nine days
years.p: Four pieces of about 20 minutes each, recorded at Chemical Sound in Toronto in February 2000 with Daryl Smith, from material the band had been playing live. Constellation's vinyl comes October 9, Kranky's CD October 23.
years.xp: The Village Voice called it the best movie it had seen all year. Pitchfork put it fifth for 2000 and 65th for the decade.
play: Lift Your Skinny Fists Like Antennas to Heaven

yt: Full show, Bagnolet near Paris, January 2002
years.h: A war chart on the back of Yanqui U.X.O.
years.p: The third album is recorded in Chicago with [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]]. The back cover maps major record labels' ties to the military-industrial complex, and the liner notes tie "09-15-00" to Ariel Sharon's march on al-Haram al-Sharif.

years.big: "The whole film was cut to Godspeed in my head."
years.h: Danny Boyle cuts 28 Days Later to Godspeed
years.p: Boyle's zombie film plays an edit of "The Sad Mafioso" from F♯ A♯ ∞.
years.xp: For a lot of people, 28 Days Later was the first time they heard the band.

eras.title: Held at a gas station in Ardmore
eras.text: On tour in the States, the band's look and Canadian plates were enough for a gas station attendant to call in terrorism. A few months later Godspeed went quiet for seven years.

years.big: "It's a good thing we're nice white kids from Canada."
yt: Full show, Ridglea Theater, Fort Worth, March 14, 2003
years.h: A gas station attendant calls in terrorism on Godspeed
years.p: Police hold the band until FBI agents arrive and question them, find anti-government papers and oil-rig photos, and let them go after background checks. Efrim Menuck's verdict comes at the next show, in St. Louis.
years.xp: Nothing incriminating turned up in Ardmore, Oklahoma. Michael Moore wrote the incident into his book Dude, Where's My Country?

years.h: A hiatus "for the better part of a year" runs seven
years.p: Constellation announces the rest while members work on other bands: Thee Silver Mt. Zion Memorial Orchestra, [[Fly Pan Am|c191214c-31e6-4d26-bfa7-35be4d90d178]], HṚṢṬA, Esmerine and Set Fire to Flames.

eras.title: god's pee rolls again
eras.text: The reunion came with a joke and no apology. The second life has been busier than the first: new records, first trips to China and Australia, a Polaris Prize, and a public argument with the gala that handed it over.

yt: Storm, Grande Halle de la Villette, Paris, 2011
years.h: "god's pee has decided to roll again"
years.p: The April 9 reunion statement, written "after a decade's retreat," books All Tomorrow's Parties. Mike Moya returns; cellist Norsola Johnson declines. A full North American and European tour follows in 2011.

years.h: 'Allelujah! Don't Bend! Ascend! ends a ten-year silence
years.p: Timothy Herzog replaces drummer Bruce Cawdron. The year also brings Coachella and Pitchfork Music Festival, stages the old Godspeed would never have played.

years.h: Godspeed wins the Polaris Prize and takes on the gala
years.p: The band's statement said holding a gala "during a time of austerity and normalized decline is a weird thing to do," and called the Toyota sponsorship insane. It suggested the next gala happen in a cruddier hall.
years.xp:
The band said they'd put the prize money toward musical instruments for people in Quebec prisons.

That fall they also opened for [[Nine Inch Nails|b7ffd2af-418f-4be2-bdd1-22f8b48613da]] on the Tension tour and played Australia, New Zealand and China for the first time.

years.cap: Godspeed at Hopscotch Music Festival, Raleigh, 2015
years.h: Asunder, Sweet and Other Distress lands between tour dates
years.p: The fifth album arrives in the middle of heavy world touring. On the road the band previews new pieces that fans nickname "Buildings" and "Railroads" after the projections behind them.

years.h: Luciferian Towers makes six
years.p: The sixth record, on Constellation, keeps the reunion pace of one album every couple of years.

eras.title: Every record a statement
eras.text: Efrim Menuck calls himself an anarchist, and the recent titles leave little doubt about the politics. In 2025 the band pulled its music off Spotify over a military AI investment.

years.h: The seventh album, and a pledge signed with 600 others
years.p: G_d's Pee at State's End! arrives the year the band joins more than 600 musicians pledging to boycott Israel until the occupation of Palestinian territories ends.

years.h: Three untitled songs debut in Queens
years.p: Godspeed plays them at the Knockdown Center, six months before announcing the album they become.

years.h: A Gaza death toll becomes the album title
years.p: No Title as of 13 February 2024 28,340 Dead takes its name from the Palestinian death count in Gaza on the day it was conceived. The band tours ten countries behind it.
play: No Title as of 13 February 2024 28,340 Dead

years.cap: Godspeed at Paard, The Hague, March 2025
years.h: Godspeed pulls its catalog from Spotify over Helsing
years.p: The band removes nearly all its music from Spotify, Tidal and Deezer, objecting to Daniel Ek's Prima Materia fund backing military AI company Helsing. Bandcamp stays up.

years.h: Brazil gets Godspeed's first South American date
years.p: Thirty-two years in, the band books its first show on the continent.
